links.comparator_used: Unsimplified AI-generated responses (AI-GRs); AI-simplified responses (AI-SRs) were also compared with published expert-authored responses (PEARs)
links.outcome: Total score on the 19-item information adoption model questionnaire (acceptance) among medical professionals and pediatric patient families
links.effect: AI-SR mean total scores were 72.98 (SD 12.64) for medical professionals and 65.47 (SD 16.52) for families. AI-GR scores were 76.17 and 68.77, and PEAR scores were 72.97 and 64.18. AI-SR vs PEAR showed no significant difference (both Holm-adjusted P>.99). Simplification did not raise scores above the unsimplified AI-GRs.
links.quote: Additional language simplification did not improve acceptance in this predominantly highly educated sample, and the strong tendency to attribute materials to human authors highlights the importance of source transparency.

design_hint: LLM simplification of patient education materials (reading-level constraint)
